performers: Fyodor Chaliapin, bass; orchestra conducted by Albert Coates
intro: Song of the Volga Boatmen, in the arrangement by Chaliapin and Keneman, is a refrain once sung by men pulling barges along the Volga. Chaliapin sang the solo bass part again with Albert Coates conducting, five years after his recording with Byng.

sections.label: A · The hauling song, bass voice
sections.mNote: The work song returns, sung by Chaliapin’s bass voice.

cues.title: Refrain, solo bass
cues.text: The refrain “Ey, ukhnyem!” recurs throughout the song. In this arrangement Chaliapin sings it as a solo bass.
cues.evidence: The traditional Russian refrain and lyrics: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Song_of_the_Volga_Boatmen. Chaliapin’s voice and the orchestral arrangement are documented at https://pool.publicdomainproject.org/index.php?title=Gramophone-db1103-2-022051
cues.how: About the passage as a whole.

cues.title: Recording session, London, 1927
cues.text: Chaliapin and Albert Coates made this recording in London on 20 October 1927. The arrangement bears Chaliapin’s name alongside Fyodor Keneman’s, so the singer was also one of the arrangers who brought the work song into the concert hall.
cues.evidence: Public Domain Project, Gramophone DB 1103: session, conductor, singer and both arrangers. https://pool.publicdomainproject.org/index.php?title=Gramophone-db1103-2-022051

cues.title: Balakirev’s folk-song collection, 1866
cues.text: In 1866 Mily Balakirev published the boatmen’s tune in his collection of Russian folk songs, with only one verse. Further verses were added later, among them the address to the Volga as a mother river, wide and deep.
cues.evidence: Balakirev’s 1866 collection, the original single verse and the later text are described at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Song_of_the_Volga_Boatmen
